coverage_gaps: egvStatusId SENSOR-VALIDITY GATE IS UNCLAIMED. Verified at plugins/shipped/tandem/src/main/.../ble/messages/StatusResponseParser.kt:198-202 — `val egvStatus = cargo[6].toInt() and 0xFF; if (egvStatus !in 1..3) return null` (0=INVALID, 1=VALID, 2=LOW, 3=HIGH, 4=UNAVAILABLE), with five dedicated test cases at StatusResponseParserTest.kt:214-258. This is the sensor's own claim that the value is usable and is entirely independent of the 20..500 range check that every subsystem enumerated. The Tandem subsystem lists 'Live CGM read (EGV opcode 34/35)' as a capability but its safety_critical array never mentions the gate. A Swift port that keeps the range check and drops this one renders warm-up and error sentinels as real glucose. It belongs in the same enforcement tier as the 20..500 bound.

iobType SELECTOR (mudaliarIOB vs swan6hrIOB) IS UNCLAIMED. Verified in the ControlIQIOBResponse layout (TandemBleDriverTest.kt:67-73, StatusResponseParserTest.kt:24-40): the 17-byte cargo carries BOTH a Mudaliar IOB and a Swan-6hr IOB, and a trailing iobType byte selects which is the live value (0 = Control-IQ off, 1 = Control-IQ on). The Tandem subsystem lists 'IoB read (opcode 108/109)' as a capability and never names the selector. Picking the wrong field displays a plausible but wrong insulin-on-board number — dosing-relevant misinformation with no validation that would catch it, because both values are in range.

TREND-ARROW PROVENANCE IS UNCLAIMED. The single most-read element on the dashboard (cgmTrendIconId, 1..7 → CgmTrend) is sourced from HomeScreenMirror opcode 56/57, NOT from the CGM EGV response. The Tandem subsystem names the opcode pair in a capability title but nothing states that trend and value come from different transactions, can therefore disagree, and can be independently stale — which matters far more on iOS where the two reads may land in different background wakes.

ACCESSIBILITY AND THE UI-TEST IDENTIFIER CONTRACT HAVE NO OWNER. Verified: 253 `testTag` and 113 `contentDescription` call sites across app/src/main and wear-device/src/main, plus a CustomAccessibilityAction in MealHomeComponents.kt. Several part-2 subsystems depend on this contract without owning it (the pairing subsystem even flags a duplicated `pairing_fault` accessibility identifier as a bug to fix during the port, and CI gates proposes XCUITest as the instrumented-test successor). Nothing scopes accessibilityIdentifier parity, VoiceOver labels for the colour-encoded coverage states, Dynamic Type behaviour, or the watchOS tinted/accented complication rendering mode that flattens the alert-bell and graph colour vocabulary. On iOS this is not polish: it is the acceptance-test substrate for every Simulator-runnable gate.

LIVE ACTIVITY / ACTIVITYKIT IS PROPOSED BY FOUR SUBSYSTEMS AND OWNED BY NONE. Medtronic, pairing UX, docs, and the release subsystem all name a Live Activity as the substitute for PumpConnectionService's ongoing notification — the only backgrounded surface carrying the alert-floor honesty text (verified as three distinct strings in app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml). Nobody owns its requirements: NSSupportsLiveActivities, the ~8h active / ~12h Lock Screen expiry, user dismissibility, ActivityKit push-token updates, what happens to the honesty claim when it expires overnight, and the pessimistic-seed / never-overwrite-a-degraded-status rules that must port to it.

SHARED DATA CONTAINER AND TARGET TOPOLOGY HAS NO OWNER. Fragments appear everywhere — App Group identifiers templated on Team ID (release, pairing), 'SafetyCore must build for iOS, watchOS and the widget extension' (driver API), Keychain access groups (pairing), FileProtection class (CI gates) — but no subsystem owns the topology: which targets exist (phone app, watch app, iOS widget extension, watch widget/complication extension, N driver targets, SafetyCore, PumpDriverAPI), which of them may construct a validated reading, what crosses the App Group boundary vs WatchConnectivity, and how a per-Team-templated App Group survives a fork rebuild without orphaning the container. This is the structural replacement for the Wearable Data Layer and it is unscoped.

CRASH-REPORTING POSTURE COLLAPSES UNDER FORK-AND-BUILD AND NOBODY RESTATES IT. Android's rule (PRIVACY.md:24-28, SentryInitializer.kt, a CI GradleException if SENTRY_DSN is set) is 'no build the PROJECT distributes phones home; a developer may compile in their own DSN'. When every build is a user build, that distinction has no referent. The docs subsystem lists 'PRIVACY.md — Sentry error-monitoring posture' as a capability but its rewritten claim set (four outbound connections, no telemetry) omits Sentry entirely. Unresolved: does the iOS app link a crash reporter at all, whose DSN, does the fork template expose it as an opt-in secret, and what does PRIVACY.md then claim.

APNs IS A CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY THAT NO PART-2 SUBSYSTEM CARRIES. Server-generated alerts (caregiver alerts and anything the backend computes) cannot reach a suspended or terminated iOS app by any mechanism except APNs. The wire slot already exists — contract/openapi.json's DeviceRegistrationRequest.platform includes 'ios', and device_token is presently a locally generated UUID. Part 1 raised the trust posture as a PM question; no part-2 subsystem states the resulting requirement on the iOS side (register a real APNs token, handle a background push, reconcile against /api/v1/alerts/pending) or the corresponding dependency on the platform repository accepting per-deployment APNs configuration.

ANALYTICS SETTINGS (dayBoundaryHour + backend-synced bolus-category labels) ARE UNNAMED. AnalyticsSettingsStore.kt validates dayBoundaryHour in 0..23, is fed from ApiModels.kt:184 `day_boundary_hour`, and is consumed by HomeViewModel.kt:158-159,354 to bucket daily statistics. TIR/CGM-stats capabilities are claimed by the monitoring subsystem but the day-boundary parameter — which silently changes every daily aggregate and every 'today' window — and the category-label override map are named by no subsystem.

LOCAL STORE MIGRATION POLICY IS UNSTATED. AppDatabase.kt is at `version = 13` with two committed migration tests (Migration11To12Test, Migration12To13Test in app/src/androidTest). The iOS app starts at schema v1 with no Android data to import — that is a decision worth recording explicitly (no cross-platform data migration path; a user switching from Android starts empty and backfills from the backend or from pump history), together with the iOS store's own forward-migration policy and its test gate, which CI gates mentions only as 'the database-migration test ports'.

BATTERY / BACKGROUND-COST BUDGET HAS NO OWNER. docs/mobile/install.md:135 publishes a '< 5% per day' figure on the public site. The release subsystem says 'replace with a measured iOS figure or omit it' and nothing else scopes measuring it. Given the iOS design deliberately trades a persistent connection for connect → burst-read → disconnect cycles plus an indefinite pending connect, the battery profile is materially different and the published claim is currently unbacked for iOS.

NON-GAPS, RE-VERIFIED SO THEY ARE NOT REDISCOVERED AS SCOPE: no localization (single values/ dir, strings.xml is 6 strings, all other copy inline in Kotlin); no AppWidgetProvider, TileService, ShortcutManager, deep links, or ACTION_VIEW intent filters (grep returns nothing; MainActivity is exported with an explicit comment that it processes no intent data); no Health Connect / androidx.health; no data export or share; allowBackup=false. Consequence: every iOS widget, Lock Screen widget, Smart Stack entry and complication proposed across the fourteen subsystems is ADDITIVE SCOPE standing in for the lost Wear watch face and the lost foreground-service notification — it must be framed that way in the PRD, not as parity restoration.

plugins/example IS NOT A BUILT MODULE. settings.gradle.kts includes :app, :wear-device, :watchface, :pump-driver-api, :tandem-pump-driver, :medtronic-pump-driver — and no :example. The driver-API subsystem treats DemoGlucometerPlugin as the reference driver and recommends promoting its iOS successor (SimulatedPumpDriver + trace-replay driver) to first-class shipped targets. That is a status change from 'unbuilt sample' to 'linked into every user's binary', and it needs an explicit decision rather than inheriting the Android framing.
contradictions: CalibrationTarget vs 'no write surface exists anywhere'. The driver-API subsystem's own safety_critical array asserts 'no bolus/basal/therapeutic write surface exists anywhere in the SDK... Any port must preserve this closed capability set', while the same subsystem ports 'CalibrationTarget capability and BG validation' as a capability. Verified: CalibrationTarget.kt:25 is `suspend fun calibrate(bgValueMgDl: Int, timestamp: Instant): Result<Unit>` — a write to the device. Android's own policy (CONTRIBUTING.md:26,30 and MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md:27) explicitly permits it as non-therapeutic session/lifecycle. The iOS mandate says 'read-only'. Grep confirms ZERO shipped drivers implement it — only PluginRegistry.kt holds an activeCalibrationTarget slot. One verdict is required, and it determines whether 'this binary contains no device-write code path' is literally true.

Keychain accessibility class: the Medtronic subsystem recommends `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock` (no ThisDeviceOnly) for the pairing record. The Tandem subsystem says ThisDeviceOnly 'is mandatory so a pump pairing secret never syncs to another device via iCloud Keychain or a restored backup', the pairing-UX subsystem mandates `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` for all pairing credentials, and the CI-gates subsystem proposes a static-analysis rule that FAILS the build on 'any non-ThisDeviceOnly class for pump/auth items'. As written, the Medtronic recommendation would be rejected by the gate another subsystem proposes.

ConnectionState enum — three incompatible verdicts on one cross-target shared type. Driver API: keep exactly the seven cases, add no public case, expose Bluetooth availability on a parallel stream, emit synthetic restoration transitions. Tandem: 'Add the two distinct states BLUETOOTH_UNAVAILABLE and PERMISSION_DENIED' and 'Drop SCANNING'. Pairing UX: add distinct surfaced states. This enum is consumed by the phone app, the watch target, and the backend contract; it cannot have two shapes.

Reconnect policy — three specs for one mechanism. Pairing UX: 'Replace both phases with one permanent pending connect... Explicitly forbid any give-up-after-N logic in code review' and states that reimplementing the ladder 'would be strictly worse: more radio churn, more wakeups, no benefit'. Tandem: 'Foreground: keep the exact FAST ladder and its counters so user-visible reconnect behavior matches Android. Background: cancel timers, issue one indefinite connect()'. Driver API: a driver-owned 30 s timeout for user-initiated connect plus a never-timing-out pending connect for auto-reconnect. These produce three different user-visible behaviours and three different code-review rules.

Security-gate stack and required-check NAMES diverge four ways, and branch protection keys on the name. CI gates: rename to 'Static Analysis Gate', CodeQL Swift + Semgrep p/secrets on macOS. Contract: CodeQL Swift + Semgrep p/secrets published under the SAME name 'Security Scan Gate' specifically so the branch ruleset does not change. Docs: 'Semgrep p/swift and p/secrets, plus swiftlint --strict' — explicitly not CodeQL. Medtronic: pinned Semgrep + a repo-authored Swift rule pack + gitleaks + Swift 6 strict concurrency + MobSF. Tandem: CodeQL(swift) + Semgrep p/secrets + OSV + SwiftLint. A PRD that carries all five yields a ruleset naming a check nothing produces.

MobSF is simultaneously declined and load-bearing. CI gates: 'Decline MobSF for the same stated reasons' as Android, substituting a deterministic Entitlements & Plist Guard. Driver API: 'the substance is recovered from MobSF for iOS/Swift static analysis' — i.e. MobSF is the named replacement for the lost Semgrep Kotlin coverage. Medtronic: 'MobSF wired but advisory until a write surface exists'. Android's own documented revisit trigger for artifact SAST (introducing a write/therapeutic surface) does not fire, so the decline is the consistent verdict — but three subsystems must not each assume a different one.

Simulated-driver distribution status. Driver API, Tandem and pairing UX all want the scriptable simulated driver and the trace-replay driver as 'first-class shipped targets' runnable in the Simulator and in CI. The contract subsystem goes further and removes the Android exclusion that kept example plugins out of the safety-constant scan, on the grounds that on iOS the simulated driver IS shipped code. The provisional part-1 critic says the opposite and is right about the hazard: Android hard-gates its fault/reading injectors to BuildConfig.DEBUG at two levels because injected readings write the same cache that drives the glucose hero and can fire a real alarm. Under fork-and-build every build is a user build, so 'shipped' and 'distributed' are the same word — the PRD must state the build-configuration boundary explicitly rather than letting two subsystems mean different things by 'shipped'.

Glucose validation regime — three different accept windows for the same value, and the consolidation recommendation does not distinguish them. Verified asymmetry: Nightscout ingestion validates against ABSOLUTE 20..500; the Tandem history path validates against the user's backend-synced SafetyLimits; the Tandem LIVE CGM path (TandemBleDriver.getCgmStatus) calls parseCgmEgvResponse WITHOUT limits and silently uses defaults. The contract subsystem's flagship recommendation is to consolidate to one `GlucoseSafety.validRange = 20...500` — but SafetyLimits is a user-narrowable window, not the absolute constant, so consolidating the constant does not settle which window each source is checked against. The consequence nobody states: a backend that narrows SafetyLimits silently drops BLE readings the same app accepts from Nightscout, changing TIR, GMI, CV, the chart and the alert floor's input set.

Wrist alert transport — unresolved from part 1 and untouched by part 2. Alerting and the data layer both recommend letting iPhone system mirroring be the only wrist buzz; the wear subsystem recommends scheduling the notification ON the watch via transferUserInfo, explicitly because mirroring occurs only while the iPhone is locked. Wear is correct on the platform fact, so the other two silently accept a wrist that stays silent whenever the phone is unlocked and in use — a parity regression against a Wear service that vibrates unconditionally today.

Alert-floor arming gate 1 (server-alerting-degraded) — unresolved from part 1. Alerting recommends keeping SSE only while the process is alive and letting AlertStreamState rest at DISCONNECTED because that 'correctly arms the on-device floor via the existing degraded predicate'. The data layer says the same redefinition inverts the primary dedup layer and leaves the floor permanently armed in background. Both cannot be implemented.

Distribution-model erosion presented as convenience. (a) The release subsystem has upstream CI publish iOS and watchOS Simulator .app bundles as release assets — a project-published binary, against a 'ship source, not binaries' mandate. Unsigned Simulator bundles are not device-installable and are the lead's only run surface, so this is probably right, but it needs explicit sign-off rather than arriving as a build-artifact detail. (b) The release subsystem then asks whether the hardware validator should be added as an internal TestFlight tester on the lead's App Store Connect account — that IS the project conveying a signed GPL-3.0 binary under Apple's DPLA, and it reintroduces exactly the licence conflict the fork-and-build model exists to avoid.

Deployment-target floor stated three ways: pairing UX 'iOS 17 or later so Live Activities, .timeSensitive and Smart Stack are all available unconditionally'; docs install page 'iOS 17+/watchOS 10+ hardware'; docs CONTRIBUTING 'iOS 18 / watchOS 11 Simulator runtimes'. One number, and it gates several capability assumptions.

Deliberate user-facing deletions arriving as asides under a strict-parity mandate: the draggable meal FAB with its per-device position and VoiceOver reset action; cfg_theme and cfg_show_seconds; the SCANNING connection state; DiscoveredPump and the four deprecated pump interfaces; the pump MAC address shown in the pairing screen and Settings; and the entire watch-face surface reframed as complications. Most of these are correct calls, but each is a shipped control or contract being removed and each needs to land in a parity ledger with an explicit verdict, not inside a recommendation paragraph.

must_ask_pm.question: Under fork-and-build, no user can obtain the Critical Alerts entitlement (Apple grants it per Team ID on individual written request, and every user signs with their own personal team), so the urgent-low alarm can be silenced by the ring/silent switch — and no public API can even detect that the phone is muted. Do we ship a glucose monitor on that basis, and if so, what is the required disclosure surface and wording?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: Apple's rules and the distribution model settle the ENGINEERING answer unanimously across four subsystems (design for .timeSensitive, upgrade to .critical automatically if the entitlement is ever present). What they cannot settle is whether shipping a monitor whose most safety-relevant alert is silenceable is acceptable for this product, and where that must be stated. Android gets DND bypass and alarm-volume boost from ordinary install-time permissions (ACCESS_NOTIFICATION_POLICY and MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS, both verified in the manifest), so this is a genuine capability loss on a life-safety path, and MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md Critical Warning #4 is the highest-consequence prose in the repository.
options: Ship on .timeSensitive; strengthen Critical Warning #4, restate the supplement-not-replacement claim in onboarding and Settings, and require a one-time acknowledgement
Ship on .timeSensitive and additionally require every user to attempt the entitlement request for their own team as a documented setup step, upgrading automatically when granted
Treat guaranteed audible urgent-low as a launch blocker and hold iOS until a mechanism exists

must_ask_pm.question: Medtronic 700-series on iOS has two unknowns that can only be settled against a real 780G that nobody on the team owns, and either can make the driver impossible: whether Core Bluetooth can hand back a CBPeripheral for the pump that just connected to our CBPeripheralManager, and whether the pump's discovery filter accepts an iOS advertisement that cannot carry manufacturer-specific data. Does the project fund or recruit 780G hardware before the driver architecture is committed, and if the spike fails, does iOS ship Tandem-only?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: Parity says ship every supported device; Android's own posture (README table: 'Beta, read-only, unverified on hardware') says ship it honestly labelled and gated — that much is inferable. What is not inferable is the contingency and the spend. If the client-link handoff fails there is no workaround at any tier, so the parity mandate is simply unmeetable for that device, and the fallback (Tandem-only, or Medtronic reachable only cloud-mediated via Nightscout) is a decision about which users iOS serves at launch. It also compounds a resourcing question: one maintainer with one t:slim X2 is currently the sole validator for every BLE, background, notification and watch behaviour in the product.
options: Fund/recruit a 780G tester before committing the driver architecture; hold Medtronic scope until the spike passes
Build the offline-provable majority now, ship Medtronic present-but-gated and labelled BETA/unverified, accept the transport as unproven indefinitely
Ship iOS Tandem-only; state that Medtronic parity is not achievable on this platform
Fund a second hardware validator regardless of the Medtronic outcome, to remove the single-point-of-failure on all iOS validation

must_ask_pm.question: Is the fork's build-and-sign pipeline an upstream-maintained, supported product surface — held to the same required gates, CODEOWNERS review, and security-response commitments as the app — or reference configuration each user adopts at their own risk?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: This determines who owns the consequence when upstream workflow code executes inside a user's GitHub Actions run with that user's App Store Connect private key and signing identity in scope. Android had one project-held keystore under one person's control; iOS distributes the blast radius across every user. The answer changes the required-check set on the workflow file, whether a compromised action is a security-advisory event for the project, whether SECURITY.md's disclosure scope covers it, and how much of the pipeline can be templated versus hand-configured. It is a liability and support-scope judgment with no technical answer.
options: Supported surface: CODEOWNERS-gated, SHA-pinned, in the security-response scope, with a documented upgrade path
Reference configuration: shipped in the template, explicitly unsupported, with a stated warning that syncing upstream runs new code against the user's credentials
Supported for the workflow file only; the user's secrets, account state, and Apple relationship are explicitly out of scope

must_ask_pm.question: Does counsel need to review two GPL-3.0-only distribution questions before the fork-and-build instructions are published: (1) whether MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md's 'users become the manufacturer of their own personal medical device' framing — today reserved for third-party forks that add device control — now describes every iOS user; and (2) whether adding the hardware validator as an internal TestFlight tester on the lead's own App Store Connect account is a conveyance of a GPL-3.0 binary under Apple's Developer Program License Agreement?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: The fork-and-build model resolves the general VLC-precedent problem — a user building from source they hold and installing to their own device is not a conveyance — which is why the model was chosen. What it does not resolve is these two residuals. (1) gates the two highest-traffic published pages (the install runbook and the disclaimer) and cannot be answered from the Android repo, Apple's rules, or the product context. (2) is the fastest possible hardware-validation loop and the release subsystem asks for it directly; it also reintroduces exactly the licence conflict the model exists to avoid, and it involves third-party copyright holders in the Medtronic driver's provenance who cannot be bound by the project lead alone.
options: Counsel review before publishing; validator builds from his own fork under his own account ($99/yr, licence-clean)
Counsel review before publishing; validator added as an internal tester if counsel clears it
Publish now stating the builder relationship factually without asserting a legal conclusion, and obtain review before the first tagged release

must_ask_pm.question: Server-generated alerts cannot reach a suspended or terminated iOS app without APNs. Under fork-and-build each user has their own Apple Developer team and can mint their own APNs auth key for their own bundle ID — but that requires the platform repository to accept per-deployment APNs configuration. Does the platform team take that on, or does iOS ship with backend alerts reaching the app only while it is running?
must_ask_pm.why_it_cannot_be_inferred: The distribution model actually resolves the trust posture part-1 flagged as unanswerable — no project-operated relay and no shared signing key are needed, because each self-hoster holds their own key for their own bundle ID. What remains is a cross-repository roadmap commitment this repo cannot make. The wire slot already exists (contract/openapi.json DeviceRegistrationRequest.platform includes 'ios'; device_token is currently a locally generated UUID), so the blocker is the backend feature, not the contract. Without it, iOS loses background delivery of caregiver alerts and every server-computed alert — a real regression against Android's indefinitely-held SSE foreground service — and the on-device floor covers only glucose thresholds it can compute locally.
options: Platform repo adds per-deployment APNs config; iOS registers a real device token and handles background push
No push on iOS: SSE while the process is alive plus opportunistic pulls plus the on-device floor, documented as a known iOS-only regression
Defer: ship without push, reserve the token path in the client, revisit after the first release

safe_assumptions: Tandem live-CGM validation window (asked by the Tandem subsystem): use ONE validation regime — the user's backend-synced SafetyLimits — on every path and every source, and surface clamping/rejection events. Rationale: the divergence is an acknowledged Android defect the code itself flags as needing a deliberate decision; tightening validation is monotonically safe; and the contract subsystem's consolidation work is the moment to fix it. Record the consequence explicitly: a narrowed SafetyLimits now also drops Nightscout readings it previously accepted, which is the correct behaviour and must be visible.

Tandem Mobi status (asked by the Tandem subsystem): ship it, carrying Android's exact labelling forward — 'protocol-compatible, unverified on hardware' — and treat any Mobi bug report as hardware-blocked. Parity plus the README table's own vocabulary settle this; the iOS table simply adds a 'validated on iOS hardware by / on' column that stays empty.

Medtronic foreground-only pairing as parity (asked by the driver-API subsystem): yes. Apple's documented behaviour — background CBPeripheralManager advertising drops CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey and moves service UUIDs into an iOS-only overflow area — makes foreground-and-screen-on the only physically possible shape. Ship it that way with a keep-awake pairing modal, and state in-app and in the docs that Medtronic reconnection is best-effort. The only unresolved part is the spike contingency, which is the surviving PM question.

Stable + dev side-by-side install on one iPhone (asked by the release subsystem): not required. On iOS it costs every user a second globally-unique App ID, provisioning profile, App Store Connect record and TestFlight setup — roughly doubling onboarding — to replace something Android got free from an applicationId suffix. Use a single bundle ID with a branch-selectable build workflow; document that switching branches replaces the install. Revisit only if the hardware validator demonstrates a need to run both simultaneously.

Plaintext-HTTP LAN backend / ATS exception (part-1 question): keep the opt-in and ship a scoped ATS exception via NSExceptionDomains, with UrlSecurityPolicy's successor as the in-app guard, exactly as Android does. The risk that made this a question — standing App Review exposure — does not exist in the fork-and-build model: internal TestFlight distribution triggers no Beta App Review, and the build is signed under the user's own account. Removing the LAN-HTTP opt-in would be a parity break bought with nothing.

GPL-3.0 vs Apple's DPLA, general case (part-1 question): the stated distribution model already resolves it. A user who forks, builds from source they possess, signs with their own key and installs to their own device is not being conveyed a binary, so GPLv3 §6 and §10 do not bite — this is precisely why the Loop / xDrip4iOS model was chosen. Only the two residuals in the surviving legal question remain open.

Notification authorization: request [.alert, .sound, .badge, .criticalAlert] in ONE call at the end of BOTH onboarding completion paths (after login and after 'use without a server'), mirroring where Android requests POST_NOTIFICATIONS. iOS prompts once per install, so a later .criticalAlert request silently no-ops; requesting it without the entitlement is harmless. Never use .provisional — provisional delivery is quiet, which silently disables every alarm.

Keychain and Data Protection classes: kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly for every credential and pairing secret (AfterFirstUnlock so background reconnect authenticates on a locked device, ThisDeviceOnly so a pump pairing secret never leaves via iCloud Keychain or a restored backup), and FileProtectionType.completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication for the database — never .complete, which would fail background writes while locked. Enforce both with a static-analysis rule. The Medtronic subsystem's AfterFirstUnlock-without-ThisDeviceOnly recommendation is superseded.

ConnectionState: keep the seven cases unchanged, expose Bluetooth availability (poweredOff / unauthorized / unsupported / resetting) on a parallel stream following the existing PairingFault precedent, and emit synthetic AUTHENTICATING → CONNECTED/AUTH_FAILED transitions on Core Bluetooth state restoration. The driver-API verdict wins over Tandem's and pairing's added cases because the enum is a shared contract across the phone app, the watch target and the backend; adding platform-specific cases forks it. Keep SCANNING and finally use it during pairing.

Reconnection: one mechanism — an indefinite pending centralManager.connect re-armed on every disconnect and on poweredOn, with no attempt cap and no give-up condition, counters retained for diagnostics only. This preserves the load-bearing Android safety decision ('the pump is a medical device; if the user has not unpaired, always try to reconnect') using the platform's own kernel-serviced primitive, and a code-review rule forbids attempt caps and app-scheduled reconnect timers in the connection layer. The FAST/SLOW ladder is an Android workaround for a primitive iOS provides natively.

CalibrationTarget: omit CALIBRATION_TARGET from the v1 iOS capability set. Zero shipped drivers implement it (verified: only PluginRegistry holds the slot), so it is not a 'currently supported feature' under the parity mandate, and porting an unused device-write code path into a binary whose entire safety story is 'read-only' buys nothing. Reserve the enum case and record the omission as a deliberate divergence from Android's stated policy, which does permit calibration as non-therapeutic.

Every 'impossible' verdict is unanimous, correct under Apple's published rules, and needs no product input: runtime plugin loading and the custom-plugin install UI; in-app APK self-update and its download hardening; the wear APK push and installer; third-party custom watch faces and the face gallery; BootCompletedReceiver; foreground services; a permanently visible non-dismissible ongoing notification; setBypassDnd by application decision; alarm-volume boost; programmatic bond removal; BluetoothGatt.refresh(); requestMtu and requestConnectionPriority; advertisement manufacturer data and advertising-interval control; background advertising discoverable by a non-Apple central; and holding an SSE stream open while suspended. Accept the documented substitutes without escalation.

Localization, HealthKit, deep links, widgets-as-parity, data export and backup: no obligation. Verified absent from the Android repo (single values/ resource set with a 6-string strings.xml; no AppWidgetProvider/TileService/ShortcutManager/VIEW filters; no androidx.health; allowBackup=false). Inline Swift strings are acceptable parity. Do NOT add HealthKit write — it would create a therapeutic-adjacent data path with no Android counterpart.

Number formatting: Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX") with explicit .rounded(.toNearestOrAwayFromZero) before formatting, everywhere, and ban .formatted() and unpinned NumberFormatter on glucose values by lint. Java's %.0f rounds half-up while C/Swift printf rounds half-to-even, so formatMean(72.5) differs; pin the tie cases in tests. Scope string-equality tests to en-US Android output plus the cross-surface glucose fixtures; do not reproduce Android's comma-decimal behaviour for IoB/TIR/CV/GMI, which is a defect.

Bolus-history BG column: fix it (convert and label per the user's unit) and log it as a deliberate documented divergence. Parity means feature parity, not defect parity, and shipping an unlabelled mg/dL integer to an mmol/L user on a clinical surface is the exact desync class the drift guard and the Medical-Safety review gate exist to prevent.

cfg_theme and cfg_show_seconds: delete — verified dead on Android (validated, stored, read by nothing). Record as a verified no-op so it is not later mistaken for a regression. The draggable meal FAB: replace the drag, the persisted per-device position and the VoiceOver reset action with fixed bottom-trailing placement plus a redundant 'Log a meal' row; the drag exists only to compensate for an Android occlusion problem. Keep every availability gate exactly.

Wrist alert transport: schedule the alert notification ON the watch from a WatchConnectivity wake, not via iPhone mirroring. iOS mirrors to the Watch only while the phone is locked, so the mirroring designs accept a silent wrist whenever the phone is in use — a parity regression against a Wear service that vibrates unconditionally. A watch-local re-buzz ladder is also strictly better than Android, and must terminate once the underlying reading ages past TOO_STALE with a final 'data is stale, nothing is watching' notification.

MobSF / artifact SAST: decline, consistent with Android's own recorded decision, and carry its revisit trigger verbatim (reinstate if distribution changes or any write/therapeutic surface is introduced — neither fires). Substitute the deterministic Entitlements & Plist Guard, which covers the posture class Android Lint covered with no false-positive tax.

Build number: derive CFBundleVersion from a monotonic UTC clock value plus a never-decreasing per-fork offset variable, not from the Actions run number. Run numbers regress when a user recreates a fork or archives locally first, and App Store Connect then permanently rejects uploads for that marketing version. Do not reproduce Android's packed versionCode formula — it carries a silent collision bug at patch > 9999.

Upstream may publish unsigned iOS and watchOS Simulator .app bundles as release assets. They are not device-installable, cannot be signed by the project, and are the lead developer's only run surface given he has no iPhone or Apple Watch. This does not breach 'ship source, not binaries' in substance, but state it explicitly in the PRD so it is a decision rather than a build-artifact side effect.

SwiftPM pinning: commit Package.resolved, pin dependencies exactly, and build with automatic package resolution disabled so a stale lockfile is a hard failure. This is the sharpest silent trap in the port — SwiftPM's default is to quietly re-resolve when the manifest and lockfile disagree, which defeats both pinning and any dependency scan that reads the lockfile.

Domain-type validation style: throwing initializers for the four validating domain types (so boundary tests can assert min, max, min−1, max+1) plus a failable convenience initializer used by every parser and BLE ingestion path, so an out-of-range reading is dropped and logged. Ban precondition/fatalError on any value originating from BLE, the backend, or persistence by lint — a trap inside a Core Bluetooth callback during a background restoration launch kills the process invisibly and gets the app deprioritised for future relaunch.
top_port_risks: CRITICAL — Medtronic may be unimplementable on iOS at the transport layer, and it cannot be proven either way. There is no documented API to obtain a CBPeripheral for the central that just connected to your CBPeripheralManager (retrieveConnectedPeripherals and retrievePeripherals-by-identifier are both undocumented for this purpose), and iOS cannot emit the manufacturer-specific advertisement the pump's matcher was reverse-engineered against. Either failure makes the entire read layer unreachable even after a successful SAKE handshake. Nobody on the team owns a 780G. Everything below the transport is offline-provable; nothing at the transport is. Mitigation: one probe app answering both questions in a single hardware session, ahead of any parser work, behind a MedtronicPumpLinkResolver seam.

CRITICAL — roughly 10,400 LOC of safety-critical BLE protocol and crypto with no Apple-platform library underneath it. Tandem EC-JPAKE needs raw P-256 point addition and arbitrary-base scalar multiplication that CryptoKit does not expose; Medtronic needs a clean-room Swift reimplementation of the JVM-only JavaSake six-stage handshake, the SeqCrypt per-direction sequence cipher, and AES-CMAC, which build.gradle.kts itself notes the JCE lacks and CryptoKit also lacks. A subtle error — a wrong encoding length, a mis-reduced ZKP hash, an unblinded scalar — produces a handshake that fails only against real pump firmware, which the lead developer cannot reach. Mitigation: port the existing tools/medtronic-ble-spike captured-trace harness to Swift FIRST, add Kotlin↔Swift differential vectors with a seeded RNG, and validate on a macOS bench (CoreBluetooth is fully available on macOS) before any iPhone work.

CRITICAL — no background execution guarantee, so the on-device alert floor and the honest-coverage claim become conditional on Core Bluetooth producing wake events. Android's foreground service polls every 15 s forever, which doubles as the ~30 s BLE keep-alive; iOS suspends between callbacks, BGAppRefreshTask is opportunistic at ~15 min or worse, and a poll-only peripheral generates no wake events at all. Compounding, all invisible while they happen: force-quitting from the app switcher permanently disables Core Bluetooth relaunch until manual reopen; nothing runs after reboot until first unlock; Low Power Mode removes the backfill path. Mitigation is architecture plus honesty — connect → burst-read → disconnect cycles with an indefinite pending connect, history backfill on every wake, a persisted last-successful-wake timestamp, and a prominently visible data-age everywhere.

CRITICAL — the urgent-low alarm is silenceable and the app cannot detect it. Critical Alerts is unobtainable per-user under fork-and-build; .timeSensitive breaks through Focus but not the ring/silent switch, and neither the switch position nor the ringer volume is readable by any public API. Android gets both from install-time permissions. This does not merely degrade a feature — it undermines the honest-coverage architecture the whole alerting design exists to protect, on the single most safety-relevant path in the product.

HIGH — the entire BLE, background, notification and watch surface is validated by one person on one device. Core Bluetooth does not exist in the iOS Simulator (CBCentralManager reports .unsupported); the lead developer has no iPhone and no Apple Watch; the sole hardware maintainer has a t:slim X2 and no Medtronic hardware. Worse, the Simulator produces false positives on exactly the properties that matter: it does not validate entitlements, does not enforce Local Network Privacy, does not enforce Keychain lock-state or Data Protection semantics, has no Focus or ring switch, does not honour WidgetKit / WatchConnectivity budgets, and does not faithfully simulate suspension. A written, gated on-device smoke checklist is the only validation for the life-safety path.

HIGH — the three cross-repo safety constants have no owner and iOS multiplies the surfaces. 20..500 mg/dL is duplicated across ~19 enumerated sites (including 20..499 and 21..500 off-by-one variants and a SQL BETWEEN literal), 18.0156 across two, and TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET = 1199145600 in one — held equal only by a comment-stripped source scan that has no iOS counterpart. iOS adds a watch app, an iOS widget extension, a watch complication extension and an App Group boundary. The epoch offset is the worst of the three: getting it wrong shifts every pump timestamp by the device's UTC offset (Foundation has no LocalDateTime, so the UTC-decode-then-reanchor step does not port literally) and silently destroys the freshness, staleness and coverage architecture everything else rests on.

HIGH — Kotlin-to-Swift translation of validation and parsing has two failure modes, both worse than Android's. A literal transcription of `require` to `precondition` traps the process — a crash inside a background Core Bluetooth restoration wake that the user never sees and that gets the app deprioritised for relaunch. Clamping to avoid the trap fabricates a plausible glucose or dose. Alongside: Swift traps on integer overflow where Kotlin wraps (the CRC loop, the 8-bit txId, a Mobi uint32 exceeding Int32), Data slices carry a non-zero startIndex so an index-based parser silently reads wrong offsets after the first slice, and Double→Int on NaN traps. Enforce all four by lint plus fuzz tests over truncated and random payloads.

HIGH — Codable silently breaks the tolerant reader in the direction the contract ADRs depend on, and fork-and-build makes the unproven direction normal. Swift's synthesised decoder throws .keyNotFound for a non-optional property with a default value, so every Kotlin DTO field carrying a constructor default converts from tolerant to hard-failing — visible only against an older backend, which upstream CI never exercises. Simultaneously, because each user builds from an arbitrary commit against a self-hosted backend of arbitrary age, the newer-app → older-backend direction that ADR 0002 explicitly does NOT establish becomes the common case rather than an edge case.

HIGH — bond removal is impossible and peripheral identity is unstable, so trust failures strand users permanently. All three Tandem recovery paths and both drivers' unpair paths call removeBond(), which has no iOS equivalent at any tier; recovery becomes a manual Settings → Forget This Device procedure plus physical access to the pump's pairing menu. Meanwhile CBPeripheral.identifier is per-app-install, so a reinstall, a bundle-ID change, or a device migration silently loses the binding — and fork-and-build users reinstall constantly because TestFlight builds expire every 90 days. Mitigation: persist the pump serial as the durable identity, re-bind on serial match, and port Android's counter-based restraint policy faithfully (never invalidate after a successful session; tolerate 20 consecutive encryption failures).

HIGH — insulin records can be lost through history-cursor bugs that iOS makes far more likely. Medtronic's bolus cursor is process-local, unpersisted, and advances before the orchestrator persists — tolerable on Android only because a durable Room-backed slow loop self-heals. Tandem's history cursor lives only in memory and its opcode-58 firstSeq/lastSeq are record INDICES, not sequence numbers, with deduplication resting entirely on a unique-timestamp index. iOS terminates apps routinely, so both cursors must become durable before either fast path ships, and the durable path must be the source of truth for insulin totals.

HIGH — fork-and-build distributes the supply-chain blast radius across every user's Apple Developer account. Package.swift is executable Swift evaluated at resolve time, SPM build-tool plugins run during build, and Xcode Run Script phases execute on every build — all inside a job that holds the user's App Store Connect key and signing identity. Android had one project-held keystore under one person's control. Mitigation: a mechanical Build Script & Plugin Guard over project.pbxproj and Package.swift against a CODEOWNERS-owned allowlist, checksum-pinned binaryTargets (or none), full SHA pinning throughout the fork workflow, and an explicit statement in SECURITY.md that syncing upstream runs new code with the builder's credentials.

MEDIUM-HIGH — a name-only port of the security gates yields required checks that are permanently green and test nothing. Semgrep's p/kotlin and p/java packs produce exactly zero findings on Swift, and no Swift ruleset of comparable depth exists from any vendor. Copying the workflow by tool name would manufacture false assurance on a health-data app. Compounding: SwiftPM advisory coverage in OSV and the GitHub Advisory Database is a small fraction of Maven's, so the dependency gate will be green far more often than it is correct. Mitigation: CodeQL Swift as the blocking analysis with a seeded finding proving it can fail the build, a non-zero-rule-count canary, both OSV and Dependabot, and a deliberately tiny dependency surface as the primary control.

MEDIUM-HIGH — the honest-coverage claim loses its permanence guarantee. Android's foreground-service notification is unconditional, undismissable and always present, with lastFloorStatus caching existing specifically so a redundant service start cannot overwrite 'Alerts degraded — this phone is NOT watching for lows or highs' with reassuring copy. iOS has no undismissable persistent notification: a Live Activity is user-dismissable, ends after ~8 hours active and ~12 hours on the Lock Screen — so a degraded state can silently vanish from every out-of-app surface overnight, which is precisely the window the app exists to cover.

MEDIUM — TestFlight builds stop launching 90 days after upload. For a diabetes monitor that is a silent, total loss of monitoring, not a cosmetic degradation, and it has no Android analogue (a sideloaded APK simply keeps running). Mitigation: a scheduled rebuild workflow enabled by default in the fork template, plus in-app build-date/expiry/days-remaining and escalating local notifications.

MEDIUM — watchOS complications render in an accented/tinted mode that flattens hue, and the alert-bell complication encodes its entire six-branch coverage-honesty decision in grey/amber/red while the graph encodes basal, bolus, activity bands and glucose banding entirely in colour. A literal port makes 'everything is fine' and 'your phone is dead and nothing is watching' pixel-identical — deleting the dead-phone cue in exactly the case it exists for. Re-encode on SF Symbol, shape and text before writing any complication view and gate on greyscale screenshots of all six branches.

MEDIUM — macOS runners are ~10× private-repo minutes and queue slower, and every required build gate must move there. That cost pressure is the most likely reason someone weakens a gate. Mitigation: keep the fork public, factor platform-agnostic parsing and safety logic into SwiftPM targets tested with `swift test` on Linux, keep workflow-lint and workflow-security on ubuntu, and add explicit timeout-minutes to every job.
prd_section_recommendations: **Safety Invariant Register** — a numbered table of every invariant that must survive the port, each with: the invariant, its current Android enforcement, its iOS enforcement mechanism (type system / test / lint / review), its owner, and its cross-repo coordination rule. Must include the three drift-guarded constants (18.0156, 20..500, TANDEM_EPOCH_OFFSET = 1199145600), drop-never-clamp, the two independent bolus caps and the milliunits-vs-units ×1000 scale, the egvStatusId 1..3 gate and the iobType selector (both currently unclaimed), reservoir-is-whole-units, and the SafetyLimits-read-current-not-cached rule. A generic PRD produces requirements; this product needs a register because the invariants are duplicated across ~19 sites with no owner and the guard that keeps them equal has no iOS counterpart yet.

**Per-Device Verification Matrix and Status Vocabulary** — an iOS-independent device table with a 'validated on iOS hardware by / on date' column, plus definitions of what each status word means and what gating each implies (ship enabled / ship gated off / not present). MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER.md defers to this table as the authoritative safety status, so it cannot be inherited from Android: an iOS BLE stack is different code, and a carried-over 'Verified' would be a false safety claim about software nobody has run. It also makes the Medtronic and Mobi scope decisions legible as data rather than prose.

**Validation Tier Model** — four named tiers (Simulator + simulated driver, trace-replay against recorded pump frames, macOS bench against a real pump, on-device hardware smoke) with, for each: what it can prove, what it cannot, and which release action it gates. Must include the explicit list of properties ONLY hardware can prove — entitlements, Local Network Privacy, Keychain lock-state semantics, background wake and Core Bluetooth state restoration, WidgetKit/WatchConnectivity budgets, Focus and the ring/silent switch, watch haptics. This section exists because Core Bluetooth is absent from the Simulator, the lead has no iPhone or Watch, and the Simulator produces false positives on exactly the properties that matter; without it, 'tests pass' means something different to every reader.

**Parity Ledger** — a three-column ledger of every divergence from the Android product: forced losses (platform-impossible), deliberate divergences (chosen improvements or defect fixes), and additive substitutes (net-new work standing in for something lost). Each row carries a verdict and a rationale. The mandate is strict parity, so every deletion of a shipped control (draggable meal FAB, cfg_show_seconds, the SCANNING state, the displayed MAC) and every reframing (watch face → complications; widgets as substitutes for the foreground-service notification) must be an explicit decision rather than an aside inside a recommendation paragraph.

**Capability Surface Closure and its Mechanical Enforcement** — the exact protocol set the driver API exposes, what is deliberately excluded and why (CalibrationTarget, with the note that Android's own policy permits it as non-therapeutic and zero shipped drivers implement it), and the API-surface snapshot gate that turns 'read-only' from a review rule into a build failure. The read-only posture is the top-level safety architecture and the single strongest claim the project makes; on iOS it is also the claim most worth being able to prove about the shipped binary.

**Alert Delivery and Honest-Coverage Contract** — the coverage-claim vocabulary, every surface that carries it (in-app banner, Live Activity, complication, notification), the permanence problem now that no undismissable surface exists, the pessimistic-seed and never-overwrite-a-degraded-status rules ported to each surface, and the explicit non-guarantee language for Critical Warning #4. Includes the Critical Alerts absence and its disclosure requirements. This is the highest-consequence prose in the product and it currently exists as three strings in strings.xml plus a caching rule — it needs to be a specified contract, not an implementation detail.

**Distribution and Build-Lifecycle Requirements** — per-user identifier and entitlement provisioning (App IDs are globally unique across all Apple accounts, so nothing can be shared), the fork's secret contract, signing property assertions replacing Android's fixed-fingerprint check, build-number monotonicity, the 90-day TestFlight expiry and its automated-rebuild requirement, and an explicit statement of what upstream may and may not publish. Android needed none of this — an applicationId is a string and a keystore is a file. This is the single largest new setup burden in the product and the most likely source of user-reported 'bugs' that are actually provisioning failures.

**Shared Data Container and Target Topology** — the full target list (phone app, watch app, iOS widget extension, watch complication extension, SafetyCore, PumpDriverAPI, one target per driver, simulated and trace-replay drivers), which targets may construct a validated reading, what crosses the App Group boundary versus WatchConnectivity, the templated-per-Team App Group and Keychain access group, and the build-configuration boundary that keeps a fabricated-glucose source out of the configuration a user uploads to TestFlight. This is the structural replacement for the Wearable Data Layer and it is currently specified only in fragments across five subsystems.

**Cross-Repo Contract and Compatibility Directions** — the pinned OpenAPI, CONTRACT_VERSION, the endpoint-presence and field-presence coupling (including the nullable-consumed exception, Nightscout pump_events.units, whose silent absence drops events and understates IOB), the two compatibility directions ADR 0002 establishes, and the fork-and-build consequence that the unproven third direction is now the normal case. Also carries the APNs dependency on the platform repository. A generic PRD assumes one deployable stack; this product is a client for a self-hosted backend of arbitrary age built from an arbitrary commit.

**Security Gate Substitution Table** — Android gate → iOS gate → what coverage is lost → what compensates, with the required-check NAMES fixed, because branch protection keys on them and four subsystems currently propose four different stacks and two different names. Must state plainly that Swift static-analysis depth is materially thinner than Kotlin/Java and that the compensating controls are type-level invariants, replay tests and a deliberately tiny dependency surface — not a renamed tool.

**Public Documentation Boundary and Namespace Plan** — docs/** publishes to glycemicgpt.org merged into one namespace with the platform repo, which means a third repo creates direct basename collisions (mobile/install.md, troubleshooting/cant-pair-pump.md, daily-use/connecting-medtronic-pump.md) that nothing in any repo detects, since there is no link checker anywhere. Also specifies which pages are legal statements requiring review before publication (install runbook, PRIVACY, MEDICAL-DISCLAIMER, the device table) and which claims are architecturally enforced versus prose — a distinction that matters far more when the project cannot verify what any installed binary contains.

**Community Driver Contribution Path** — one SwiftPM target per device, explicit DriverCatalog registration with a CI test asserting the exact expected plugin-ID set (Swift cannot enumerate protocol conformances, so a driver that compiles but is unregistered is silently absent — a failure mode Hilt's @IntoSet prevents on Android), per-driver dependency lint replacing the deleted runtime sandbox, CODEOWNERS review, and a mandatory field naming who will validate the driver on which physical hardware. The last item has no Android counterpart and is now mandatory, because nothing BLE is testable in the Simulator and a contributor cannot validate their own driver.

**Accessibility and UI-Test Identifier Contract** — accessibilityIdentifier parity for the 253 existing testTags (they are the acceptance substrate for every Simulator-runnable gate), VoiceOver labels and non-colour encodings for every state currently carried in colour alone, Dynamic Type behaviour on the glucose hero and complications, and the watchOS tinted/accented rendering requirement. Currently owned by no subsystem while being depended on by several.

**Crash Reporting and Telemetry Posture under Fork-and-Build** — Android's rule ('no build the project distributes carries a DSN; a developer may compile in their own') has no referent when every build is a user build. Specify whether the iOS app links a crash reporter at all, whose DSN, whether the fork template exposes it as an opt-in secret, what scrubbing is mandatory if so, and exactly what PRIVACY.md then claims. Left unstated, this becomes a privacy claim that quietly stops being true.
